subject: Performance sizing and token headroom — post-demo recap
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Alex Marin <alex.marin@veloxhealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 11 Jan 2027 15:18:00 -0800
Subject: Performance sizing and token headroom — post-demo recap

Thanks again for the demo time today — appreciate the context on the triage workflow. Two quick recaps and asks so we can size a POC: 

Summary notes from our side:
- Target latency: you mentioned end-to-end responsiveness matters for triage. Can you confirm the p50/p95 goals you want for short (<=512 tokens) and long (>=1500 tokens) flows?
- Typical payloads: you said average input context is ~1k tokens, expected output ~300 tokens, but there were long transcripts occasionally. Please confirm percent distribution if possible.
- Concurrency & throughput: rough peaks you expect during batch triage windows and sustained concurrency.
- Streaming: you indicated streaming is required for the patient-facing triage path — we'll prioritize a streaming-capable config in the POC.

Immediate asks / next steps:
1) Can you share a small sample of 200 prompts (redacted) and a short histogram of input/output token lengths?
2) We will produce a mutual action plan and a recommended canary config (model + quantization + routing) that optimizes for your latency SLOs and token headroom. Expect a draft M.A.P. by EOD Thursday.
3) Clarify fallback behavior for requests that exceed the max-context threshold (should we truncate, switch to a summarizer pre-step, or route to a paid long-context model?).

Attachments: mutual-action-plan.xlsx (draft template), velox-example-prompts.txt (example prompt formatting).

Irene

Date: Tue, 12 Jan 2027 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Performance sizing and token headroom — post-demo recap

Irene — great walkthrough, thanks. Below are the numbers you asked for (high level):

- Token distribution (approx): median input ~1,100 tokens, mean ~1,250, 75th pct ~1,600, long-tail (~5%) at or above 2,000 tokens. Output: median ~250 tokens, mean ~380, very long outputs (~2% of calls) up to 2,500 tokens.
- Percent of calls that need the full transcript/context vs. summary: ~70% need full recent dialog (last 1k tokens). The other 30% tolerate a 1–2 paragraph summary.
- Concurrency/throughput: baseline sustained concurrency ~8 requests; peak concurrency during shift changes ~40 concurrent; average RPS across the day ~0.5–1.
- SLO targets: for the triage UI we want p95 response time <= 1.0s for the majority of interactions (short/medium), and p95 <= 2.5s for long-context requests — streaming for the UI is preferred so the clinician sees tokens as they generate.

On fallback: preferred approach is to try a summarizer pre-step for >2k token inputs when latency matters, otherwise route to a long-context model if the user checks the "full-analysis" box.

Happy to share the sample prompts — we'll drop a redacted set into the Drive link above by EOD.

—Alex

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Jan 2027 13:45:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: Velox sizing notes and suggested canary

Internal notes (do not share externally yet):
- Given Alex's distribution, we should optimize for the 1–1.6k token band (covers ~75% of traffic) with a fallback for the 2k+ tail. Proposed canary: 2 x gpt-j-quant nodes (bf16/8-bit mix) + 1 x long-context model (gpt-neox-20B-long) reserved for the tail.
- Routing policy:
  * token_estimate <= 1600 -> low-latency pool (quantized inference, aggressive batching)
  * token_estimate > 1600 and user flag "full-analysis" -> long-context pool (higher mem, slower p95 but supports 4k tokens)
  * token_estimate > 2000 and latency-sensitive -> run summarizer pipeline (fast model, then short-context pass).
- Caching: implement prefix KV caching for repeated patient histories to shave 15–25% off p95 on warm requests.
- Streaming: enable streaming on the low-latency pool and on long-context pool when model supports it. We may need to disable continuous batching for streaming-critical flows.

Infra ask: can infra provision 2 dedicated NODES for the canary (estimated 8 A100-equivalent GPU hours reserved) to meet Alex's peak concurrency of 40 while staying within their budget? If not, we show a degraded p95 curve to set expectations.

I'll draft the MAP and include the fallback decision matrix. Karthik

Alex — thanks for the quick numbers and the Drive drop — we got the redacted prompts. Confirming next steps and timeline: 

1) POC kickoff: propose Wed 1/20 or Thu 1/21 for a 60-minute technical kickoff (we'll bring infra + perf + solutions). Which works for your team?
2) Deliverables before kickoff: draft mutual-action-plan.xlsx, our proposed canary config (model selection, quantization, routing rules), and a simple test harness for your redacted prompts so you can run local pre-tests. We'll share those tomorrow (EOD PT).
3) Fallback behavior: we'll default to summarizer pre-step for >2k latency-sensitive calls, with an opt-in route for long-context model when the user requests full analysis. We'll include toggles in the MAP for quick A/B.

One operational note: streaming + low-latency continuous batching are often at odds — we'll include two variants in the canary and recommend the streaming-enabled pool for clinician UX.

If sounds good I'll lock Wed 1/20 10:00 AM PT for kickoff and send a calendar invite + DocuSign for the POC SOW.

Best,
Irene
